contract.rules:
If the maximum temperature recorded at Los Angeles (CLILAX) for Sep 18, 2026, is between 74-75° fahrenheit according to The Weather Company, then the market resolves to Yes.

Not all weather data is the same. While checking a source like AccuWeather or Google Weather may help guide your decision, the official and final value used to determine this market is the maximum/minimum temperature as reported by the Weather Company.

Reading weather data
Preliminary Weather Company data may be subject to rounding and conversion differences from the final reported value.
Use caution when interpreting preliminary Weather Company readings.

If it is determined in the sole discretion of the Exchange that there is a material error in the initial non-preliminary publication, Expiration may be held until the publication of a non-materially-erroneous data revision or until the Expiration Date, whichever comes first. If no data is available at the end of this period, all markets will resolve to the last fair price determined by Kalshi. Please note, a status of "Final" on weather.com/kalshi is provided for convenience only, and does not guarantee data to be error-free and thus exempt from the above.

payload.rationale: The NWS same-day forecast for September 18 predicts a high of 79 °F with mostly sunny skies at LAX. The target range is 74-75 °F, which is 4 to 5 degrees below the forecast. While coastal temperatures at LAX can be difficult to predict precisely due to the unpredictable nature of the marine layer, a same-day forecast of 79 °F with mostly sunny conditions makes a high in the mid-70s highly unlikely. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is that the forecast is 79 °F, which is well above the 74-75 °F range, meaning the true probability might be even closer to 0. The strongest reason it could be too low is that the marine layer might unexpectedly fail to burn off, keeping temperatures significantly cooler than forecasted and causing a forecast bust.
uncertainties: Recorded source limitations and unresolved future event.
